choices.content: A nonpositive number (a negative number or \(0\))

question.prompt: If a rational number \(a\) satisfies \(|a|=-a\), which type of number must \(a\) be?

solutions.explanation: \(|a|=-a\) means that the absolute value of \(a\) equals its additive inverse. This holds only when \(a\leq0\), so \(a\) is nonpositive (note that \(a=0\) also satisfies the condition).
solutions.title: Apply the absolute-value sign rule
